senses.sense_definition: A leaf, especially when referred to in botanical or pharmacological contexts.

examples.text: The herbal supplement is extracted primarily from the dried <w>folium</w> of the plant.
Each medicinal compound was carefully prepared using walnut <w>folium</w> gathered during the spring.

senses.sense_definition: A leaf or sheet in an ancient manuscript or codex, comprising two pages (recto and verso).

examples.text: The archivist carefully turned the fragile <w>folium</w> to inspect the faded script on the reverse side.
A damaged <w>folium</w> was removed from the codex for delicate restoration work.

senses.sense_definition: A sheet or page in an official registry that records a legal transaction or title.

examples.text: The registrar opened a new <w>folium</w> to record the transfer of the estate to its rightful owner.
Every transaction regarding the parcel was carefully noted upon the corresponding <w>folium</w> in the ledger.

senses.sense_definition: A registered certificate of title in land-registration records.

examples.text: When the land was sold, the existing <w>folium</w> was closed and a replacement was issued.
The legal clerk inspected the <w>folium</w> of the register to confirm the current ownership of the property.

senses.sense_definition: A thin sheet, plate, or layer of mineral in foliated rock.

examples.text: Under high magnification, each mineral <w>folium</w> displayed a distinct parallel alignment within the metamorphic rock.
The geologist measured the angle of each <w>folium</w> visible along the weathered face of the cliff.

senses.sense_definition: A lobe or segment in a branching biological structure or organ.

examples.text: The anatomical study described each distinct <w>folium</w> observed within the branching renal structures.
A single <w>folium</w> may fuse at its tip with adjacent tissues during early development.

senses.sense_definition: A leaf-like fold, ridge, or lobule on the surface of the cerebellum.

examples.text: A cerebellar <w>folium</w> consists of a central core of white matter covered by cortex.
Nerve fibers ran parallel along the main axis of the <w>folium</w> in the posterior vermis.

senses.sense_definition: A curve of the third order that has two infinite branches sharing an asymptote and forming a leaf-shaped loop.

examples.text: In geometry class, the professor graphed the classic <w>folium</w> of Descartes to illustrate loop singularities.
The algebraic properties of this symmetric <w>folium</w> were first investigated in the seventeenth century.

senses.sense_definition: A purple, red, or blue dye obtained from the turnsole plant, formerly used in manuscript illumination.

examples.text: Medieval illuminators prepared rich purple ink by mixing <w>folium</w> with egg white.
Chemical testing revealed that the vibrant violet background on the parchment was produced with <w>folium</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A distinct, symmetrical, leaf-shaped marking found on the dorsal abdomen of certain spiders.

examples.text: The arachnid is easily identified by the dark, notched <w>folium</w> running down its abdomen.
Specimens of this species show considerable variation in the color and border of the abdominal <w>folium</w>.
